construct: HNPP is usually caused by a recurrent deletion involving PMP22 that reduces PMP22 dosage. PMP22 haploinsufficiency disrupts peripheral myelin and predisposes to recurrent focal neuropathies after compression or minor trauma.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Recurrent focal neuropathies after compression, autosomal dominant family history, demyelinating physiology, and a PMP22-containing 17p11.2 deletion identify HNPP; the causal dosage effect is PMP22 haploinsufficiency.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: PMP22 duplication points to CMT1A, whereas MFN2 dysfunction produces an axonal CMT phenotype; dystrophin and sodium-channel mechanisms do not fit recurrent pressure palsies.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The deletion is explicitly given, so reduced PMP22 dosage is uniquely determined rather than inferred from phenotype alone.
